key_insight: SCAPS-1D modeling shows that a Cu2NiGeS4 absorber with In2S3 electron transport and MoTe2 hole transport layers can substantially improve thin-film solar-cell performance through band and defect engineering.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design targets for optimizing layer thickness, doping, interfaces, and resistance losses in earth-abundant chalcogenide photovoltaics.
method: Simulated an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 solar-cell stack in SCAPS-1D.
Evaluated band alignment, electric fields, carrier profiles, and recombination behavior.
Swept key parameters including thickness, doping, defect density, resistances, temperature, and illumination.
evidence_signal: The optimized device is predicted to reach 28.44% PCE with VOC = 0.984 V, JSC = 34.39 mA/cm², and FF = 84.04% at AM1.5G and 300 K, outperforming the 6.25–21.17% range cited for prior CNGS devices.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm material quality, interface stability, and real-world process tolerance.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
